newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat futures edge up in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat futures edge up in quiet session.

text.p: Australian wheat futures rose slightly in relatively subdued trading as the market waited on the monthly U.S. crop report to be issued Tuesday night.
January 1997 slipped by 50 cents to A$148.00 a tonne in two trades, but May 1997 rose A$1.50 to A$154.00 in five trades and July 1997 also rose by A$1.50 to $155.50 in five trades.

"Wednesday's trade's going to tell the story," said Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures Ltd. "If (the monthly U.S. crop report) is bullish then there's a good chance we've bottomed and that US$3.60 (a bushel) support line will hold. If it's bearish, look out."
The market was expecting some bearish news, based on larger U.S. bean and corn crops, but much of that was likely to have been factored into the market by now, Hillary said.
Trading was expected to remain relatively quiet until the crop report, he added.
Australia's harvest was progressing amid much talk about downgrades but the extent of any downgrades remained to be seen, he said.
